summary: God told each Israelite family to sacrifice a perfect lamb and put its blood on their doorframes. That night, the judgment would pass over every house marked by the blood.

story_reel.narration: God told Moses that one last plague was coming, the most serious of all. The firstborn son in every Egyptian home would die. But God gave His people a way to be safe. 'Every family must choose a lamb,' God said. 'It must be a perfect lamb with nothing wrong with it. On the fourteenth day of the month, at twilight, sacrifice the lamb. Then take some of its blood and paint it on the sides and top of your doorframe. That night, roast the lamb and eat it with flat bread made without yeast and with bitter herbs. Eat it with your sandals on your feet, your belt fastened, and your walking stick in your hand, ready to leave in a hurry!' Then God said, 'The blood will be a sign. When I see the blood, I will pass over you.' This night would be called the Passover, and God's people would remember it every year. Many years later, Jesus would be called the Lamb of God. Just like the blood of the lamb protected God's people, Jesus' sacrifice on the cross rescues everyone who trusts in Him.

scenes.caption: One last plague
scenes.art_direction: Moses speaking to the Israelite elders by lamplight, serious faces.

scenes.caption: A perfect lamb
scenes.art_direction: A family choosing a spotless white lamb from the flock; kids petting it gently.

scenes.caption: Blood on the doorframes
scenes.art_direction: A father painting the doorposts with a hyssop branch at twilight; marks shown simply as red lines.

scenes.caption: Ready to go!
scenes.art_direction: A family eating roasted lamb and flat bread while standing, sandals on, staffs in hand.

scenes.caption: Passed over
scenes.art_direction: A soft protective light covering every marked door in the village.

scenes.caption: The Lamb of God
scenes.art_direction: The doorframe dissolves into the shape of a cross on a hill at sunrise.

memory_verse.text: Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed in our place.

identity_focus.core_truth: I am saved because Jesus, the Lamb of God, took my place.
identity_focus.reflection_prompt: The lamb's blood kept God's people safe. Jesus is called the Lamb of God. How does it make you feel that Jesus took your place?

quiz.question: What kind of lamb did each family need to choose?
options: A perfect lamb without any blemish
quiz.explanation: Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male a year old.

quiz.question: Where did they put the lamb's blood?
options: On the doorframes of their houses
quiz.explanation: They put the blood on the two doorposts and on the lintel of their houses.

quiz.question: How did God tell them to eat the Passover meal?
options: Dressed and ready to leave in a hurry
quiz.explanation: They were to eat with belts fastened, sandals on, and staff in hand, in haste.

micro_prayer.text: Yahweh, thank You for the Passover lamb that kept Your people safe. Thank You even more for Jesus, the Lamb of God, who took my place. I'm so grateful. Amen.

companion.message: I remember that night so clearly: the smell of roasting lamb, my sandals on, everyone ready. And the red marks on every door. We trusted God, and He kept us safe.

review.notes: Sensitive: the coming death of Egypt's firstborn is stated (Exodus 11:5; 12:12) as the reason for the Passover sign. Lamb sacrifice is described simply. Confirm tone.
